dict.GUI_CANVASSCREEN_TXTON_BEYOND_THE_ORBITA:
Beyond the orbital graveyard, millions grapple with the reality that Earth is gone for good. Colonies eye each other across the gulf of space. Amid the embarrassment of riches that is the System's raw resources, food rations and oxygenators are suddenly more valuable than an entire freighterhold of iron and nickel. In the darkness, lines are drawn.

As a captain, keep your ship running and your crew happy, in a future Solar System where Earth is inaccessible, and corporations have more rights than people.

Resemblance to anyone real or otherwise is merely coincidence.) Flashing lights (The world and interfaces contain flashing colors which may be dangerous to those with photosensitive epilepsy.) Mature Topics (The game contains references to topics such as death, blood, injury, violence, drugs & alcohol, occult, coercion, corruption, and imprisonment.) dict.GUI_CANVASSCREEN_TXTNS_TWENTY_YEARS_AGO_:
Twenty years ago, the Earth died.

The Kessler event transformed Earth's orbital space into a typhoon of debris and space junk, lethal to anything occupying or transiting orbit. Unknown numbers perished in the fallout, as worldwide networks collapsed, and meteorites ravaged the surface. A decaying planet pushed well beyond its breaking point.

Some, like Philip Kindred, fight for meaning, and survival, amid the ruins of civilisation, scavenging, looting, taking to barbarism with disquieting ease. The furthest they can see is the next day, and they'll count themselves lucky to see it.
dict.GUI_CANVASSCREEN_TXTON_OTHERS_LIKE_THE_M:
Others, like the millions waiting for word on Mars, Venus, and Saturn's moons, grapple with the reality that Earth is gone for good. Colonies eye each other across the gulf of space. Amid the embarrassment of riches that is the System's raw resources, food rations and oxygenators are suddenly more valuable than an entire freighterhold of iron and nickel. In the darkness, weapons are drawn.

You're the captain of a spaceship, one of few who hold their destiny in their own hands. In these desperate times, you must decide whom you can stand to trust, keep them close, and above all, keep your ship flying ... (this ending call to action is intentionally vague and we should adapt it to what gameplay elements we want to highlight)
